probes.query: An older client posts spans in the legacy JSON format, where one record describes a whole RPC using client-send and server-receive timestamps. Which code turns that single record into separate client and server spans that share one span id?
expectedFacts: The legacy HTTP upload route decodes with SpanBytesDecoder.JSON_V1, whose list decoding calls V1JsonSpanReader.readList, which calls V1SpanConverter.convert for each v1 record.
When the converter sees both a client-send and a server-receive annotation, it produces a client span and a server span; the server span is marked shared and takes its timestamp from server-receive.
If client and server have the same service name (loopback), the converter forks a new span builder for the server side instead of reusing the client one.

probes.query: On the Elasticsearch backend, how does a trace search with service, tag and duration filters first find the matching traces and then return complete traces rather than only the matching spans?
expectedFacts: getTraces first sends a filtered search (time range, service, remote service, span name, _q tag terms, duration range) with a terms aggregation on traceId limited to the requested number and ordered by the minimum timestamp descending.
The resulting trace IDs are passed through GetSpansByTraceId, which issues a second search over the same daily indices for all spans whose traceId is in that list.

probes.query: When the server is configured to trace itself, how do its own spans reach the configured storage, and what stops the act of saving them from producing more traces?
expectedFacts: LocalSender.send decodes each JSON-encoded span and calls the storage span consumer's accept(...).execute() directly in-process, with no HTTP hop.
LocalSender.delegate looks the StorageComponent bean up lazily and, when it is a TracingStorageComponent, unwraps it to the underlying storage, so the flush is not itself traced.

TracingStorageComponent wraps storage calls in TracedCall spans for reads and writes; the Tracing bean uses NEVER_SAMPLE and only the HTTP server sampler starts traces (for paths under /api or /zipkin/api).

probes.query: With the MySQL backend, how is the service dependency graph answered when the precomputed daily link table has no rows?
expectedFacts: When storage Schema is first built (lazily, once), HasPreAggregatedDependencies.test counts rows in zipkin_dependencies and sets hasPreAggregatedDependencies only if there is at least one.

probes.query: Legacy log messages arrive over a raw TCP socket as length-prefixed frames, possibly many at once. How are those frames cut, decoded into spans, and kept in order in the replies?
expectedFacts: NettyScribeServer installs a LengthFieldBasedFrameDecoder (4-byte length prefix, stripped) in front of ScribeInboundHandler.

ScribeInboundHandler.channelRead wraps each frame as an HTTP thrift request to a THttpService and numbers it; a response is written immediately only if its index is previouslySent+1, otherwise it is parked in pendingResponses and flushed in order by flushResponses.

ScribeSpanConsumer.Log skips entries whose category differs from the configured one, base64 (MIME) decodes the ISO-8859-1 message, decodes a Thrift span with SpanBytesDecoder.THRIFT.decodeOne, then calls collector.accept on the blocking executor.

probes.query: Cassandra storage keeps tables of known service and span names. How does it avoid issuing an insert for the same pair on every batch of spans?
expectedFacts: CassandraSpanConsumer builds insertServiceSpan as an InsertEntry.Factory (a DeduplicatingInsert.Factory) with the autocomplete TTL and cardinality, and accept() calls insertServiceSpan.maybeAdd for each (service, span) pair.

maybeAdd only creates the insert call when DelayLimiter.shouldInvoke returns true; the DelayLimiter suppresses the same context until its TTL expires, bounded by a maximum cardinality where the eldest suppression is evicted.

probes.query: When more storage writes are in flight than the write throttle allows, where is the rejection actually produced, and what decides how many writes may run at once?
expectedFacts: The number of concurrent writes is the size of a ThreadPoolExecutor whose core and max sizes follow a Gradient2Limit, resized by ThreadPoolExecutorResizer whenever the limit changes.
The limiter is a NonLimitingLimiter whose acquire always returns a listener, so the limit's own concurrency check never rejects.
Rejection comes from the executor's bounded LinkedBlockingQueue: its rejection handler throws the RejectedExecutionException "STORAGE_THROTTLE_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE reached".

probes.query: Why do responses listing service names sometimes carry cache headers and sometimes not?

probes.query: When the default in-memory store is full, which stored spans are dropped to make room?
expectedFacts: doAccept computes how many spans must be recovered (current + incoming - maxSpanCount) and calls evictToRecoverSpans before adding the new spans.
deleteOldestTrace removes the trace whose timestamp key is last in the descending-by-timestamp map, i.e. the oldest, including all its spans.

probes.query: If the same span is reported twice to the Elasticsearch backend, why does it not end up as two documents?
expectedFacts: BulkIndexWriter.write returns the document ID as the trace ID, a hyphen, and the MD5 hash of the serialized JSON document.
BulkCallBuilder.writeIndexMetadata puts that ID in the bulk index action's _id field, so an identical span overwrites the same document.
A span whose content differs in any serialized field (for example an extra tag) gets a different ID and is stored as a separate document, to be merged at read time.

probes.query: Where does the server accept trace exports sent in the OpenTelemetry wire protocol (OTLP over HTTP or gRPC)?
expectedFacts: The repository has no OTLP receiver; the only gRPC ingestion route is /zipkin.proto3.SpanService/Report in ZipkinGrpcCollector, which decodes Zipkin proto3 spans with SpanBytesDecoder.PROTO3.
HTTP ingestion routes are /api/v1/spans and /api/v2/spans in ZipkinHttpCollector, accepting Zipkin JSON, proto3 or Thrift only.
The only mention of OpenTelemetry in Java sources is an unrelated StringUtils import in PulsarCollector.

expectedFacts: The repository has only head-style sampling: CollectorSampler decides per span from the trace ID hash (debug spans always kept), applied in Collector.sample before storage.
Nothing buffers a trace until complete before deciding; self-tracing uses Brave samplers for the server's own requests.
The search space contains no error- or latency-aware keep/drop policy.
